questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have been studying English for five years and I am improving slowly.
I have been studying English for five years and I am improving slow.
I have been studying English for five years and I am improving slowly.
I have been studying English for five years and I am improving slowest.
questions.answer: I have been studying English for five years and I am improving slowly.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect tense?
options: She has lived in London since 2010.
She lives in London since 2010.
She has lived in London for 5 years.
She is living in London since 2010.
questions.answer: She has lived in London since 2010.

questions.question: Select the correct comparative form.
options: Which is the more interesting book?
Which is the more interesting books?
Which is the more interesting bookes?
Which is the more interesting book's?
questions.answer: Which is the more interesting book?

questions.question: Choose the correct conditional sentence.
options: If it rains, we will stay home.
If it rains, we would stay home.
If it rains, we will stayed home.
If it rains, we have stayed home.
questions.answer: If it rains, we will stay home.

questions.question: Which modal verb is appropriate for giving a promise?
options: I will do it.
I can do it.
I might do it.
I must do it.

questions.question: Select the correct form after 'remember to' in the past.
options: I remember to post the letter yesterday.
I remembered to post the letter yesterday.
I remembered to post the letter yesterday.
I remembers to post the letter yesterday.
questions.answer: I remembered to post the letter yesterday.

questions.question: Choose the correct gerund or infinitive.
options: I enjoy painting.
I enjoy to paint.
I enjoy paints.
I enjoy painting.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect continuous tense?
options: I have been living here for ten years.
I was living here for ten years.
I have lived here for ten years.
I am living here for ten years.
questions.answer: I have been living here for ten years.

questions.question: Select the correct option to complete the sentence.
options: Although he is tired, he continues working.
In spite he is tired, he continues working.
Even though he is tired, he continues working.
Despite he is tired, he continues working.
questions.answer: Although he is tired, he continues working.

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence?
options: The museum is very popular with tourists.
The museum is very popular to tourists.
The museum is very popular for tourists.
The museum is very popular by tourists.
questions.answer: The museum is very popular with tourists.
